name_reason: Name follows the data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention: domain 'chapter', descriptor 'per_chapter_category_table' accurately reflects both purpose (per-chapter story/battle category flag) and data type ('table' = array). No Ghidra address residue in the name. The 30 dimension is a legitimate domain count (30 chapters) and need not appear in the name.
purpose: Per-chapter story/battle category flag table; indexed by chapter id (0..29) to branch the chapter-transition and save/load flows between story-chapter handling (intro panel + save/load menu) and battle-chapter handling.
logic_summary: 30-entry const byte table. Element value 0 = story chapter, nonzero (1) = battle chapter. All three consumers read it as byte ptr[chapter_id] and branch on ==0. fd2_chapter_transition_menu indexes by data_fd2_chapter_current_chapter_id (disasm: CMP byte ptr [EAX+0x526b9],0 with EAX=current_chapter_id). fd2_save_current_state_to_slot uses it to decide whether to show a 'saved' confirmation dialog (story chapter only). fd2_load_state_from_selected_slot indexes by the slot's stored chapter byte to gate restore: empty slot re-prompts, battle-chapter slot shows an error dialog (text 0x1DF), story-chapter slot restores (text 0x1DE). Values: indices 22,23,24,27,28,29 = 1 (battle chapters; 1-based chapters 23,24,25,28,29,30, e.g. final boss chapter 30); all other indices = 0. Matches src initializer and live memory bytes exactly.
element_semantics: One byte per chapter (index = chapter id 0..29). 0 = story chapter (intro panel + save/load menu flow); nonzero = battle chapter (direct dialog + recruitment flow). Confirmed against fd2-knowledge: index 29 (chapter 30) is the final boss battle, index 0 (chapter 1) is a story/shop chapter.
notes: src comment (chtab3.c lines 16-20) already precise and correct (indexing 0..29, 0=story/nonzero=battle, three named readers, read-only, @0x526B9); left unchanged so chtab3.c is NOT modified. Ghidra data plate was empty (<null>); created a concise PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline+cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,...) reflecting the src conclusion. const confirmed: all 3 xrefs are [DATA] reads, disasm shows only CMP byte ptr reads, no game-side writer. Name kept (no rename needed, so nothing for Stage 2).
